subject: Hosting warranty, bastion access and private-peering proof pack
messages:
From: Olivia Price <olivia.price@cedarhealth.com>
To: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@cedarhealth.com
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:17:00 -0800
Subject: Request: hosting warranty and bastion details for SOC 2 review

Hi Sean,

Thanks for the demo last week — CedarHealth is preparing for a SOC 2 gap assessment and our security team asked for a short pack to validate region hosting and private deployment controls. Could you provide the following items so we can complete the SIG/CAIQ mapping?

1) A one-page hosting warranty that states the region commitment (US-only for production, with fallback in US-west region), SLA exceptions, and the scope of data residency.
2) A VPC/private-link diagram showing peering/egress paths and where tenant traffic terminates (PNG preferred).
3) Bastion/jumpbox runbook that describes access model, MFA, session recording and how ephemeral creds are rotated.
4) A statement on KMS partitioning or key separation for customer tenants, and whether HSM-backed keys are available.
5) Any supporting CAIQ/SIG attachments and the SOC 2 control mapping you maintain for private deployments.

If possible we need the pack and a signed hosting warranty (DocuSign) by Friday so the assessors can proceed Monday. Procurement is cc'd to align on signature routing.

Thanks — appreciate the help.

Olivia Price
Security Program Manager
CedarHealth

Attachments: none
From: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Request: hosting warranty and bastion details for SOC 2 review

Olivia — thanks for the clear list. We're aligned and can deliver a concise proof pack. High-level plan:

• Hosting warranty (attached PDF v1) that commits production workloads to US regions only (we include a fallback region policy; production failover remains within US geographies).
• VPC diagram (attached PNG) showing privatelink endpoints, peering to customer peering appliances, and explicit egress hops.
• Bastion runbook (attached MD) describing role-based access, MFA via SSO, ephemeral session tokens, and centralized session recording retention (90 days default, can be adjusted per contract).
• KMS statement in the warranty: tenant key separation via customer-specific key namespaces; HSM-backed KMS available for Dedicated/Private tier.
• CAIQ/SIG snapshot and SOC 2 control index — we'll provide a redacted CAIQ export for private deployments (sensitive bits omitted) and a mapping spreadsheet.

Irene and Karthik are looped for technical confirmation and any legal-friendly wording. We'll upload the accompanying artifacts to a shared Drive and send a DocuSign link for the hosting warranty.

Deliverables attached: hosting_warranty_v1.pdf; privatelink_vpc-diagram.png; bastion-access-runbook.md
Drive: https://drive.google.com/host_warranty_doc
DocuSign draft: https://na1-docsign.example/ds/ABCD1234

Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 08:25:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: hosting warranty and bastion details for SOC 2 review

Hi Olivia — technical follow-up from security/compliance. Thanks Sean for the initial pack. A few clarifications and proposed wording changes to ensure alignment with audit expectations: 

1) Hosting warranty: we've included a targeted clause that production tenant data will reside in US regions only; we cannot offer absolute geo-lock guarantees for all metadata (routing metadata may transit control planes during autoscaling). Proposed wording: "Redwood Inference commits that customer production workloads for CedarHealth will be provisioned and persisted within the United States. Administrative/operational telemetry may transit control-plane locations for management purposes; customer data at rest is restricted to US-hosted persistent stores"

2) KMS: we support per-customer key namespaces. For Private deployments we can offer HSM-backed key material and export policies. For Hosted (multi-tenant) we provide strict key separation and SOC 2 controls over key access. We'll include the KMS access log snippets in the CAIQ appendix.

3) Bastion/jumpbox: Access model is SSO + short-lived jump tokens (30m default). All sessions are recorded and stored in an immutable log. Access is audited quarterly and access reviews can be produced on request. We recommend CedarHealth request a named admin list for emergency privileged sessions to expedite incident response.

4) Egress/fallback: We can guarantee failover remains within US regions (primary region: us-east-1; fallback: us-west-2). We cannot commit to a single AZ residency. If CedarHealth needs per-AZ guarantees we'll need Dedicated/Private deployment with contractual language.

5) SOC 2 / CAIQ: karthik will attach a CAIQ export and a SOC 2 control index mapping for the privatedeploy configuration. Some SIG answers are vendor-sensitive; we will provide a redacted version and a reviewer NDA if needed.

Next steps I propose: finalize the warranty wording below and we'll push the DocuSign envelope. If procurement requests redlines, please send them back to me and legal will turn fast.

— Proposed warranty excerpt —
"Redwood Inference will provision and retain production customer data for CedarHealth within United States regions. Redwood will operate a private peering and VPC architecture for private deployments; for hosted deployments, logical tenancy and encryption controls are applied to separate customer data. Redwood will make commercially reasonable efforts to prevent cross-border data egress. In the event of regional capacity exhaustion, Redwood will failover to an alternate US region and notify the customer within the SLA window"

I can attach KMS policy snippets and a sample audit log export once you confirm.

Thanks,

Irene Choi
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.com

Attachments: (will send KMS log snippet and CAIQ extract on confirmation)
From: Olivia Price <olivia.price@cedarhealth.com>

Subject: Re: Request: hosting warranty and bastion details for SOC 2 review

Irene / Sean — this is very helpful, thanks. The proposed warranty excerpt addresses most of our assessor concerns. A few quick asks before we route to procurement for signature: 

• Can you add an explicit sentence that "administrative access to customer-managed keys is restricted and logged; key material is not exportable without customer consent"? That will close a control the assessor flagged.
• For the bastion runbook, can you confirm retention of session recordings is immutable for at least 90 days and exported in a format our auditors can replay?
• Please attach the redacted CAIQ and the SOC 2 control index in the same Drive folder so I can hand them to the assessor.

If you can drop those three items into the Drive and update the PDF (hosting_warranty_v1.pdf -> hosting_warranty_v1b.pdf) we'll route it for signature. Procurement asks whether a single signer from Redwood (VP Legal or Head of Security) can sign — procurement prefers a named signatory.

If you can get this done by EOD Monday we should be fine for the assessment window Wednesday. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,

Olivia Price
Security Program Manager
CedarHealth
